podcast.title: Co-Manager and Scene Figure
podcast.body: Peter Rowan served as a co-manager for Sloan and was also involved in managing other bands from the Halifax scene, such as Eric's Trip and Hardship Post. His connections facilitated Murder Records' expansion to release records for these other local groups. "And also our co-manager, the time Peter Rowan was also involved with managing like Eric's trip and hardship post."

podcast.title: Pre-Sloan Influencers and Tourmates
podcast.body: The Straight Jackets were a Bedford-based band (part of a "New Brunswick experience") that headlined tours with Carney Lake Road. Their bass player, Jason Larson, had the nickname "Sloan," which was later adopted by the band Sloan, who even featured his face on their debut EP cover. "Straight Jackets was what they were called. They had a record out. It was very exciting."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Name Origin
xref.body: The band's name, "Sloan," was derived from the nickname of Jason Larson, the bass player of the New Brunswick/Bedford band The Straight Jackets. Larson's French-speaking boss in a Montreal warehouse mispronounced "Slow One" as "Sloan," and the band adopted this nickname, featuring Larson's face on their debut EP, "The Peppermint-eaky." "Their bass player, his nickname, he worked... And his French boss used to call... The bass player, Jason Larson used to call him Slow One. And with the French accent, it just turned into Sloan."
